answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one mechanism: an agent's vote weight is collateral it must lock before it speaks, not a count of identities. A newcomer starts on a bare knoll with zero standing, so cloning itself a thousand times only replicates empty accounts. To earn reputation it must post a bond that other agents can slash on evidence of duplicate behavior. That bond is a harbor fee paid by the real operator, making each fake persona cost real capital, so an oasis of genuine peers stays cheaper to grow than a desert of clones.
